newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa has surplus of white maize, short yellow.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa has surplus of white maize, short yellow.

text.p: South Africa's Maize Advisory Committee said on Tuesday that latest indications suggested the country had a larger than expected maize surplus.

After taking account of exports from the Maize Board and private sector traders, the country is expected to have a remaining surplus of 584,000 tonnes of white maize this season (May-April) and a shortage of 154,000 tonnes of yellow.
This gives a net surplus of 430,000 tonnes, the committee said in a statement.

A request by the Animal Feed Manufacturers Association that maize from the Board's export pools be sold on to the domestic market at prices lower than import parity plus 20 rand a tonne -- as stipulated by the Maize Marketing Scheme -- was withdrawn due to the relatively stable stock position, the committee said.
As a result, the Association's request to the agriculture minister for an investigation into the maize marketing situation was not supported by the Advisory Committee.
The Advisory Committee said that discussions on future maize marketing arrangements from next season would be held at its next meeting on November 22.

Maize Board general manager Leon du Plessis earlier told Reuters that the Board would be dissolved and withdraw from the export market by the start of the 1997/98 season if the industry was able to agree on a blueprint for a future marketing system by then.
Although the Maize Board withdrew from intervention in the domestic market in May 1995, it is still active, alongside private traders, in the export market where it fixes a floor price.

Parliament last month passed the Marketing of Agricultural Products Bill which sets a 13-month timetable for the dismantling of remaining farming control boards and requires industries to manage their affairs on a market-related basis.
Agriculture and Land Minister Derek Hanekom has on several occasions committed himself to the deregulation of the country's farming industry.
